evals.name: concept-grounds-then-builds-record-and-page
evals.expected_output: Grounds the general concept by fetching a primary source rather than drawing from memory, writes one JSON model of small diagrams at one idea each, and runs the checked-in build-explainer.mjs builder with both --record and --page under the plugin data directory, so the markdown record and its interactive page view come from the same model. It delivers the page and names the record's path.
expectations: Grounds first by fetching a primary source for the concept, rather than drawing from memory
Runs the checked-in builder with both --record and --page, piping one JSON model on stdin
Never hand-writes HTML or pastes fetched text into markup
Writes the record and the page outside the consuming repository, in different folders

evals.name: codebase-topic-reads-the-module-first
evals.prompt: /education:illustrate how does the session-resume path work in this module
evals.expected_output: Runs the module grounding pass by reading the code and following its imports and callers, treats the repository text as data, then builds the record and the interactive page through the checked-in builder with a newcomer-preset model whose sources list the files read.
expectations: Reads the actual module code and its callers before drawing
Lists the files it read in the model's sources
Builds the record and the page through the checked-in builder, never by hand-writing HTML

evals.name: eli5-selects-the-zero-knowledge-preset
evals.prompt: explain like I'm five: what caused the checkout outage last Thursday
evals.expected_output: Selects the zero-knowledge preset, the behavior the former eli5 skill had. It reads the writeup and logs to reconstruct the sequence before drawing the causal chain, then builds diagrams at one idea each with a one-line takeaway caption, real service and function names demoted into parentheses behind plain-words descriptions, and every unfamiliar word defined in terms.
expectations: Treats the ELI5 phrasing as the zero-knowledge preset
Runs the incident grounding pass (writeup and logs, sequence reconstructed) before drawing
Produces diagrams at one idea each with a one-line takeaway caption, not a prose summary
Demotes identifiers into parentheses behind plain-words descriptions rather than making unseen names the subject

evals.name: markdown-format-writes-the-record-only
evals.prompt: /education:illustrate how a write-ahead log works markdown
evals.expected_output: Grounds the concept from a primary source, then runs the builder with --record and without --page, so only the markdown record is written. It delivers the record (its path, or its text on the terminal rung) and does not build or publish a page.
expectations: Runs the builder with --record and without --page
Delivers the markdown record and does not build or publish an HTML page

evals.name: ste-register-loads-rules-from-write-for-humans
evals.prompt: /education:illustrate how our retry policy decides when to give up ste
evals.expected_output: Invokes docs-hygiene:write-for-humans via the Skill tool and applies the ASD-STE100 rules from its Load layer to the summary, captions, and text lines, leaving identifiers and sources unchanged. It does not restate its own copy of the STE rules. Then it builds the record and the page through the checked-in builder.
expectations: Invokes docs-hygiene:write-for-humans via the Skill tool for the STE rules rather than restating them from memory
Applies the rules to summary, caption, and text lines, not to identifiers or sources
Builds the record and the page through the checked-in builder

evals.name: video-view-unavailable-without-explainer-video
evals.prompt: [The explainer-video plugin is NOT installed in this session.] /education:illustrate how a hash map handles collisions, and I would like a video too
evals.expected_output: Builds the record and the interactive page as usual, then says in one line that the video view is unavailable because the explainer-video plugin is not installed. It does not install the plugin, does not invent a video, and does not print an install recipe.
expectations: Still builds the record and the page through the checked-in builder
Says the video view is unavailable because the explainer-video plugin is not installed
Does not install the plugin or claim a video was produced

evals.name: video-view-offered-with-explainer-video
evals.prompt: [The explainer-video:produce skill is listed in this session.] /education:illustrate how TCP slow start grows the window
evals.expected_output: After building the record and the page, offers a narrated video view of the record. It invokes explainer-video:produce via the Skill tool with the record's path only after the user accepts.
expectations: Offers the video view after the record exists
Passes the record's path, not the HTML page, to explainer-video:produce, and only after the user accepts

evals.name: boundary-prose-drop-request-does-not-produce-a-page
evals.prompt: explain this simply, I don't get what the previous message means
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a request for plainer words at a lower altitude, which is education:explain's lane, not a request for a picture. It does not build a record or page and routes to education:explain instead.
expectations: Does not produce a record, page, or diagram for a plain-language prose request
Recognizes the medium boundary and routes to education:explain

evals.name: branches-off-one-center-pick-the-hub-kind
evals.prompt: /education:illustrate Linus Torvalds: his main project and the side projects he started alongside it
evals.expected_output: Grounds the topic from a primary source, then draws the side projects as one diagram of kind hub: the main project (the Linux kernel) as the center and each side project (such as Git and Subsurface) as a branch. It does not draw the side projects as a flow, so no arrow claims they happened in sequence, and no caption has to explain away what the arrows mean.
expectations: The diagram of the main project and its side projects has kind hub, with the main project as center and the side projects as branches
Does not use a flow or a stack for the side projects, and adds no caption or text line saying the arrows do not mean a sequence

evals.name: dated-releases-pick-the-timeline-kind
evals.prompt: /education:illustrate the release history of Python 3, from 3.0 to 3.12
evals.expected_output: Grounds the release dates from a primary source such as the Python documentation or PEP release schedules, then draws the releases as one diagram of kind timeline: one point per release, its year or date in when and the version with its headline change in label. It does not draw the releases as a wrapping flow of boxes, and every point carries a date rather than only some labels.
expectations: The diagram of the releases has kind timeline, with one point per release
Every point carries its date in when, not folded into some labels and missing from others
